text.p: Sugar crushing is now getting underway on a commercial basis in Brazil's north and northeast producing region, a leading analyst said.
"From this week crushing will move into full capacity levels," said Aloisio Sotero of consultants DataNet-AgriCommodities.
Brazil's north/northeast should this year crush 48.5 million tonnes of sugarcane in the 1996/97 season, up 2.5 percent on 1995/96's 47.4 million tonnes, the analyst said.
Regional crushing capacity is 55 million tonnes of sugarcane, he said.
One market source in Maceio however estimated the crush could be as much as 10 to 15 percent higher this year.
The region's sugar harvest started in August and is expected to continue until February or March.
For that reason it is still early to estimate the size of the harvest, Sotero said. The climate has been favorable to the harvest, he added.
"But both sugar and alcohol output will be slightly greater this year than last," he said.
Current expectations are that the north/northeast region will produce 3.35 million tonnes of sugar, of which some 1.75 million tonnes will be exported.
In addition, the area will produce some 1.8 billion liters of alcohol for domestic consumption, he said.
Crushers' production costs have meanwhile risen an average of 23 percent this year, reducing margins, Sotero said.
"Manpower and sugar cane costs have gone up and interest rates are high," he said.
Between now and the end of October the crushers will be fixing their sales prices, he said.
Average export price of demerara sugar is currently put at 11.60 - 11.80 cents per lb fob Recife or Maceio, the region's two major sugar ports, just one cent lower than a year ago, Sotero said.
No shipping problems are meanwhile foreseen during the current harvest at either Recife or Maceio.

A spokesman for Recife port said everything is ready for the sugar-exporting season, close contact is already being maintained with crushers and shipments should start to be programmed as from mid-September.
In 1995, Recife shipped 1.29 million tonnes of sugar, of which 742,809 tonnes was bulk and 548,721 tonnes in bags.
A spokesman for Maceio port said the port expects this year to export more than the 200,000 tonnes it shipped during 1995.
Sugar shipments from last year's harvest continue to leave from Maceio. In late August a cargo of 10,000 tonnes of raw sugar from Goias was loaded at Maceio for export to the US.
The ship Prosperity has just called at Recife to load sugar and is currently at Maceio to load 11,000 tonnes of demerara sugar from last year's harvest, bound for the US, he said.
-- Diana Kinch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
